title: How to check whether a UK job offer qualifies for Skilled Worker sponsorship
summary: Check who actually sponsors you, what the job involves, the pay and hours, and whether the dates fit. Use this checklist before accepting or paying anything.
content:
# How to check whether a UK job offer qualifies for Skilled Worker sponsorship

Last updated: 2026-11-26

## Get the job details in writing
Ask the employer for the legal sponsor, full duties, proposed SOC 2020 occupation code, basic gross annual pay, paid weekly hours, start date and CoS timetable. Check the duties against the official occupation entry. A high-sounding title, a degree or a code picked only to get a lower going rate does not make the vacancy eligible. If a recruiter is involved, ask who employs you and who would assign the CoS. A worker filling an ongoing routine role for a third party raises separate sponsorship restrictions. Check the exact arrangement before relying on it. [Job and sponsor checks](#guide-evidence-duties)

## Compare the floor and going rate
On the usual standard Skilled Worker option A, the offer must meet both £41,700 and the applicable full going rate. Under ordinary new entrant option E, compare both £33,400 and 70% of the applicable going rate. Use the correct table and hours. For tables based on 37.5 hours, adjust the going rate to the sponsored hours. The general annual floor does not go down just because you work part-time. Use qualifying pay, generally guaranteed basic gross pay. Bonuses and overtime cannot make up a gap. Health, education, shortage-list and transitional cases can have different rules. [Salary rules](#guide-evidence-pay) · [Detailed salary tables and exceptions](/en/work-visa/skilled-worker-occupations-salary)

## Try the check on a fictional offer
Assume the applicable full going rate is £50,000 for 37.5 hours and the offer is for 37.5 hours, at £34,900 basic plus a possible £1,100 bonus. Standard option A needs £50,000. If the applicant qualifies for new entrant option E, 70% of £50,000 is £35,000, higher than £33,400. The offer is £100 short on eligible pay. Even a revised £35,000 basic would only pass this example's pay check. The code, sponsorship, permission history and remaining requirements still matter. [Worked pay check](#guide-evidence-example)

## Check whether new entrant applies to you
A Graduate visa alone does not settle this. Appendix Skilled Worker gives separate grounds, including eligible recent Student or Graduate history, age under 26 and some professional or postdoctoral routes. Check the exact condition and the four-year combined cap. For example, 18 months of Graduate permission plus a requested 3-year Skilled Worker grant exceeds 4 years. Earlier Skilled Worker or Tier 2 time can also count. Ask HR to check your permission dates and the actual proposed grant. If you are still a Student, being able to switch directly is a separate test. [New entrant and switching](#guide-evidence-entrant) · [Student and Graduate timing](/en/work-visa/graduate-visa-uk)

## Stop and verify before paying
A WhatsApp promise, company logo or screenshot is not proof. Find a phone number or email on the employer's official website and independently ask HR to verify the role and CoS. Do not buy a CoS. The sponsor cannot pass the new CoS fee or associated admin costs to the worker under the applicable rules. The worker may have their own visa fees. Keep messages and receipts and use official fraud reporting if needed. If there is no confirmed sponsor or valid route as expiry approaches, seek regulated advice and follow the expiry plan. [Costs and reporting](#guide-evidence-fraud) · [Options before expiry](/en/work-visa/uk-options-after-graduation) · [Keep looking for sponsored jobs](/en/work-visa/find-uk-jobs-with-visa-sponsorship)
